David Moore, 25, lost control in a fit of road rage after leaving his home. He quickly got stuck in heavy traffic and ended up face to face with Rafal Cegielka, 45, who was picking up his child from St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire. The court heard that Moore punched Cegielka, who was on the school run, then smashed his car with a hockey stick in front of young children. The attack happened because Moore was having a bad day and became extremely angry.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday, reminding people of their poor performance at the 2014 World Cup. But defender Gerard Pique says coach Vicente del Bosque shouldn't be too worried about this third straight friendly loss. Holland had beaten Spain 5-1 in the group stage of the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, ending Spain's six-year run as the top team in world football. In this match, Holland scored two goals early at the Amsterdam Arena and managed to hold on despite strong pressure from Spain in the second half.

A mother from New York City, Ulrike Berger, 44, has run away to Germany with her seven-year-old daughter, Kaia, police say. A court has ordered her not to leave the country with Kaia. But on March 22, just one day after Kaia was dropped off for a weekend visit with her father, they are believed to have flown from New York to Germany. Police are looking for Berger and her daughter. They last saw the pair at Berger’s home in Brooklyn’s Boerum Hill neighborhood on March 21 at 10 a.m., when Kaia’s father dropped her off.

Fire roared through dry heathland near the south coast, with flames shooting high and thick, smelly smoke filling the sky. The fire destroyed a large, beautiful area—about the size of 100 football fields. This happened after several days of storms had damaged parts of Britain, knocking down trees and closing roads. But the 70-hectare area in Dorset was extremely dry because it is on a hill, and water had run off downhill. Fire investigators say the fire was set on purpose. Three separate sections of heath were burned—half a hectare, one hectare, and 70 hectares.

Emergency services got 600 calls per hour last night as people across Britain celebrated the start of 2012. Paramedics were very busy, and in Cambridge, a military field hospital was opened to help drunk partygoers. The London Ambulance Service said they had more than 600 calls in one hour, which is over three times the usual number.  
MANCHESTER: A man fell down on the sidewalk next to an ambulance while two people walked past eating a late-night takeaway.  
MANCHESTER: A man was leaning heavily against a doorway, looking very unwell, while two women passed by celebrating New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet said his mental strength helped him get through being dropped in December. He was left out of the team "indefinitely" by manager Brendan Rodgers after a bad spell of form. But he came back quickly when backup keeper Brad Jones got a thigh injury. The 27-year-old Belgian said he stayed positive even though he was upset about losing his place. Mignolet also spoke to FourFourTwo, saying, "I was positive."

Big hailstones, about the size of plums, fell over the southern U.S. on Tuesday. People ran outside to record the unusual weather. Arke USA, a Twitter user from Bryant, Arkansas, filmed the hail hitting his backyard and falling into his swimming pool. The video shows the hail falling fast, with many breaking apart when they hit the ground. Even though the temperature was about 80 degrees, the hail stayed solid for a long time and melted slowly. Within seconds, the patio was completely covered in white hailstones.

A group of nine people on a replica pirate schooner called Liana's Ransom had to leave their ship after it lost power in heavy seas off the coast of Maine. The Coast Guard rescued them on Tuesday using life boats. The ship, which is from Canada, is now floating 30 miles east of Portland. The crew reported engine problems around 12:35 a.m. on Monday. They also said the sails had gotten caught around the mast. The rescue happened at sea, and the crew members had to jump from the ship to get to the life boats.

Strange blue glowing algae have been seen along Australia’s east coast. The photos were taken in Jervis Bay, on the south coast of New South Wales, showing the bright blue light shining on a popular beach. Photographer Andy Hutchinson said the sight looked like a magical, otherworldly scene, caused by millions of tiny plankton giving off light. A similar glowing effect was seen at Sydney’s Manly Beach in August 2014. At that time, an oceanography expert told Daily Mail Australia that the algae were not harmful and there was no reason to worry.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar was drunk when he climbed into the lion enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India. He jumped over the fence and ran toward the lions, shouting that he would "kill them." He had been sitting near the enclosure when he suddenly ran into it. Zoo security had to rescue him. Afterward, he said he was drunk and thought he had a good chance of fighting the lions.

A 12-year-old boy in Nanchang, the capital of Jiangxi Province in southeastern China, survived after falling from a fifth-floor window. He landed on a car parked below the building. His father said the boy probably fell while sleepwalking. The incident happened last Saturday. A hotel worker across the street said she heard a loud noise around midnight and thought it was a car crash.

Drew Miller, a player for the Red Wings, says he's ready to play again just one day after getting a serious cut to his face. The injury could have damaged his eyesight, but he says he's lucky the skate didn’t hit his eye. At practice on Wednesday, Miller wore a full face mask and showed a deep red wound that needed 50 to 60 stitches to close. The wound ran across his face and skin, but he didn’t lose his eyesight. The Detroit Free Press reported on the injury.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid is thinking about bringing him back in the summer. He signed a three-year deal when he moved from Atletico last July, but has had trouble winning the left-back spot at Chelsea. Atletico hopes this might help them get him back, but Luis said: “I’m happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until the end of my contract.”

A Reading fan, Charlie Sumner, 20, could be banned from football for three years after he ran onto the pitch topless during his first game at the Madejski Stadium. The incident happened during the Royals' 3-0 FA Cup quarter-final replay win over Bradford City. Sumner did four front somersaults on the pitch while his team was already leading 3-0. He landed on his back and was then taken down by stadium stewards. Sumner said attending his first game was a "brilliant experience," but he now faces a possible three-year ban for his actions.

A video has been released showing a group of men riding on top of a van being thrown into the air when the van turned sharply around a corner. About six people were sitting on the roof of the van on a road near Salé, Morocco, when it tipped over at high speed. The video, filmed from a car behind the van, shows the van swerving back and forth on what looks like a busy road with two lanes in each direction. The van was likely carrying football fans.

England have been placed in Group D of the UEFA Under 17 European Championships in Bulgaria in May. They are in the same group as the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy. England are the defending champions after winning last year’s tournament in Malta by beating Holland on penalties. To reach the quarter-finals this year, England must beat Holland again. This year’s tournament has 16 teams, up from eight, for the first time. Danny Collinge celebrated by running away after scoring his first goal for England in a qualifying match against Norway.

An angry elephant sprayed water at a buffalo bull because it got too close. The elephant was resting with its family by a small pool in Kruger National Park, South Africa. When the bull came near, the elephant used water from its trunk to try to scare it away. The spray missed. The elephant tried again, but the bull stayed. The baby elephant stayed close to its parent for safety while the bull drank from the pool. The whole event was filmed.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub landlord, has had his 2006 conviction overturned after eight years. He was found guilty of showing Premier League football matches from foreign TV channels without permission from official broadcasters. The incident happened in November 2006 at the Stoke Inn in Plymouth, Devon. Mr. Thorpe, now 55, says he has suffered greatly from the long legal fight, including losing his pub.

The Irish Football Association is worried that damage to its home stadium, Windsor Park in Belfast, might affect the important Euro 2016 qualifier against Romania in June. On Tuesday morning, workers found cracks in the West Stand, which had been damaged overnight on Monday. The area was closed off while structural engineers checked the damage. An IFA spokesman said the association learned about the damage on Tuesday morning and confirmed that the West Stand at Windsor Park had been damaged during the night.

A football fan is at risk of a three-year ban after running onto the pitch at topless during his first game at the stadium. Charlie Sumner, 20, entered the field at Reading's Madejski Stadium during the FA Cup quarter-final replay against Bradford City. Reading was leading 3-0 at the time. Sumner did four front flips on the pitch, landing on his back each time, before being stopped by stadium staff.

A man driving a BMW was arrested today after a 21-year-old student, Hina Shamim, was hit and killed while walking to the library. She died near the University of Kingston in London last night, just weeks before her 22nd birthday. Hina, who was from Peterborough and nicknamed "Hyena," was well loved by friends, who left flowers at the scene. She was walking a short distance from her home when the accident happened.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video showed them fighting with a student at Langham Creek High School in Houston. The incident happened on Tuesday and was caught on camera. The mother, whose name has not been released, was said to be upset because she believed the student had been bullying her daughter. In the video, the mother is wearing a black top and is on the right side. The student who was attacked is in the center and wearing white. The video was posted online.

Stoke's chief executive, Tony Scholes, hopes the club can keep goalkeeper Asmir Begovic, who is in the final year of his contract. Begovic, a 27-year-old from Bosnia, has often been linked with other clubs since joining Stoke. Although his current contract has more than a year left, Scholes believes Stoke can meet Begovic's goals. "Asmir is a top goalkeeper, and we really want him to stay," Scholes said in an interview with The Sentinel. "When you have very good players, it's normal for people to talk about their future."

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand, was strongly criticized by his boss after being caught on video reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger filmed the driver while the bus was moving and sent the video to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines, along with a complaint. In the video, the driver is seen turning the pages of a newspaper. At a traffic light, the driver even turns his head to look closely at a page. The company’s boss, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver’s behavior and called him a "complete idiot."

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce has said Winston Reid will be fit for Saturday’s game against Leicester City, who are at the bottom of the league. Reid has been out since he hurt his hamstring in a 1-0 loss to Chelsea on March 4. He returned to full training during the international break. Enner Valencia will not play because he is still not ready. He missed the last two games against Arsenal and Sunderland after getting a strange toe injury at home in mid-March. Allardyce confirmed that Reid is back in full training.

Five days before Brittany Huber and John Redman were supposed to get married last May, a terrible car crash on a Georgia highway killed Brittany. John survived, but his body was badly injured. Doctors told him he would probably spend the rest of his life in a nursing home, unable to walk. At 25, John was an assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College, and his future seemed very dark. But against all the odds, he got better. On March 24, he helped lead his team to win a championship.

Lucas (left) and Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard were at Anfield on Sunday for a charity All-Star game. Liverpool midfielder Lucas Leiva is trying to get back to the level he played at two years ago, after recovering from injury. He had 16 starts in 19 games from late November, which matched a period when Liverpool's results improved. But a groin injury during February’s Merseyside derby caused him to miss 10 games. He did not play in the loss to Manchester United just before the international break — the first league game since mid-December. However, he played the full 90 minutes in Sunday’s charity game at Anfield.

Tired of boring father-daughter photos? One photographer has found a fun, though unusual, way to make them better. Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama's new photo series shows serious-looking teenagers standing next to their fathers, who are jumping in the air. In each photo, the daughter looks straight at the camera and smiles, while her father makes a dramatic pose. These photos are part of a new book by the 37-year-old photographer. The book's title roughly means "Daughter and Salary Man."

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old. He is suspected of stealing £3,000 in cash from a Lloyds Bank branch in Fairwater, Cardiff, during a robbery at 12:30pm. The man is 5ft 9in to 6ft tall and was wearing black clothes. He has greying black hair, wears glasses, and was seen on CCTV inside the bank. No one was hurt during the robbery. Police are confident that people in the public can help identify him.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has removed Morocco's ban from the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. Morocco was kicked out of the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and fined $1 million by the Confederation of African Football (CAF). CAF also asked Morocco to pay $9 million more in compensation, because Morocco withdrew as host due to concerns about the Ebola virus. Morocco had originally been set to host the tournament, which was won by Ivory Coast in Equatorial Guinea. Now, Morocco is allowed to take part in the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments.

Tom Boyd thinks Jason Denayer has done so well during his loan at Celtic that he is now ready to fight for a spot at Manchester City next season. This would go against Ronny Deila’s plan to keep Denayer at Celtic for another year. But Boyd sees a good side to this: Denayer’s growth shows other young players that coming to Celtic can help them move forward in their careers. The 19-year-old defender, Jason Denayer, has impressed while on loan at Celtic this season. He recently earned his first senior international cap for Belgium in a Euro 2016 qualifier against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend silenced his critics with a great goal for England. He said critics like Paul Merson helped push him to do well, especially during his time in Italy. This season has been tough for the 23-year-old, who hasn’t played as well as he did when he first joined the international team. But England manager Roy Hodgson still trusted him. Townsend showed his value by scoring England’s equalizer in a 1-1 friendly game against Italy on Tuesday night at Juventus Stadium in Turin. He celebrated the goal with his Tottenham teammates, Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Chinese property company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of Spanish football team Atletico Madrid. The deal was confirmed at an Extraordinary General Meeting on Tuesday. Wanda Madrid Investment’s legal team signed the agreement to buy 726,707 shares for €45 million (£32.8 million). The purchase was first announced in January, but two Extraordinary General Meetings were needed to complete it. Wanda Group chairman Wang Jianlin wants to expand Atletico Madrid’s brand in Asia. Atletico Madrid’s manager, Diego Simeone, is speaking to the media.

Antonio Conte said his return to Turin for Italy's 1-1 draw with England brought back "very fond memories," even though he had received death threats before the match. Conte became Italy's manager in August after the team was eliminated in the World Cup group stage. His first seven months as national team boss have been difficult and unpredictable. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to tie Bulgaria 2-2 last Saturday. Conte also reportedly received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio got a knee injury the day before the Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that a potentially easier schedule could help Hibs overtake Rangers for second place in the Championship, with just one month left in the season. His Dumbarton team has already played both of his former clubs this season and will face them again in the final weeks. Right now, Rangers are in better form — they beat Hibs and Cowdenbeath, while Hibs lost to Raith. But Murray doesn’t think this advantage will last. He believes Hibs could regain the upper hand soon. He also thinks Rangers may not be able to keep up their current pace through the final stretch of the season.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet took photos with pilots in an airplane cockpit while returning to England after playing in Belgium's Euro 2016 qualifying matches against Cyprus and Israel. Mignolet was named in the match-day squad for both games, but did not play because Chelsea goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was chosen instead. He has 14 international caps. Mignolet shared the cockpit photos on his official Facebook page on Wednesday. The photo shows Mignolet (centre) with the pilots as he comes back from international duty.

A large country estate, including a Grade II-listed manor house and five cottages, is for sale for £6 million. It sits on 200 acres of land near Bridgnorth in Shropshire. The estate has a swimming pool, tennis court, stables, and its own cricket field. The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms and was built in 1814. It has only been sold twice since then. The house, built in the Regency style, is thought to appeal to famous people because the private grounds offer full privacy. The estate is very large and includes the listed house and five cottages.

Two campus police officers at a college in Dallas have been put on leave after a video showed them mistreating a group of four students, including hitting one and arresting him. The incident happened at El Centro College in downtown Dallas. Student Charles Adams recorded the event on his phone. He was smoking a cigarette when he saw what happened. The officers approached the students while they were waiting for a bus.

Kilmarnock's interim manager Gary Locke has been made permanent after signing a three-year contract. The 39-year-old former Hearts manager joined the club last summer as assistant to Allan Johnston. He took charge of the team when Johnston left at the start of February. Since then, Locke has lost only one of his seven games in charge. He will speak to the media at a press conference on Friday morning. After signing the deal, Locke shook hands with club chairman Jim Mann.

One of the most important games in German football happens this weekend. But this year, the excitement around the match between Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich has lessened. The two teams have won the last five Bundesliga titles between them, and Bayern are expected to win again this season. This time, though, they are not close in the league table—there are 31 points and nine places between them. Still, the game is just as important as ever because it's Dortmund versus Bayern. Jurgen Klopp, the Dortmund manager, is celebrating with his players after a win against Hannover.

A 14-year-old girl was left behind at London Stansted airport after easyJet refused to let her board her flight to Spain. She was carrying two bags as hand luggage, and the airline said she couldn’t take both. Deva Joseph cried when she was told she couldn’t fly. She offered to pay to check her second bag, but the airline only accepted credit cards. She is too young to have a credit card, so she couldn’t pay.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed his grandfather, John Potts, 45, with one hard punch to the back of the head. The blow was so strong it made a loud cracking sound. The incident happened after Robson had been drinking at his grandfather’s funeral. He struck John Potts, a devoted father, outside a sports bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear, in November. John Potts fell dead. Robson had a past of violent behavior. He was sentenced to three and a half years in prison for the killing.

Scoring against your old team and making a perfect set-piece from practice are two of the best moments in football. For Notts County player Ellen White, Thursday night was unforgettable because she did both at once against Arsenal in the Women's Super League. In the 26th minute, Notts County got a free kick near the box. Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood seemed to mess up the setup, with Bassett almost running into Greenwood. This caused confusion. Then Ellen White turned near the edge of the box and kicked the free kick straight into the corner of the goal, scoring against her former team.

These are the scenes from a training session at a high school in China, where girls are practicing military-style knife moves. As they do eight specific movements, each girl shouts "kill, stab, slash, and jab." The 68 girls, all aged 16 to 18, are being trained by Inspector Tan, a former special forces soldier. The knives used are not real, for safety. A school official, Huang Anruo, confirmed that the daggers are fake.

We spend about one-third of our lives sleeping, but most people don’t pay attention to what their mind and body really need during sleep to feel rested each day. A study by the Sleep Health Foundation found that 30 percent of Australians say they don’t get enough sleep every day. Professor David Hillman, the chair, says that missing sleep must be made up to stay active and healthy throughout the week. Most adults need about eight hours of sleep each night, though seven to nine hours is considered normal.

Video has been shared online showing a fight between neighbors in a Perth suburb that turned violent with a crowbar. The video, posted on Facebook, shows an angry woman yelling racist words over her fence at a group of men she seems to think are from Africa. She then goes into her neighbor’s front yard, holds a metal crowbar, shouts at the men, and swings the tool at them. The men grab their own weapons, and a fight breaks out. The woman shouts, “I don’t deal with monkeys, go on now you f*****g monkeys.”

Everyone is watching 19-year-old left back Jose Luis Gaya from Valencia. Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea are all hoping to sign him this summer, even though Real Madrid also have interest. Pete Jenson from Sportsmail looks at the Spain under-21 player. English clubs want him because his buy-out clause is £13.5 million. That’s a lower price than Luke Shaw, who was the same age and talent level and cost £27 million. So it makes sense to be interested. But there are still concerns about whether he’s ready for the Premier League. Gaya (right) played for Valencia in a La Liga game against Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help identifying a motorcyclist who helped stop a man who allegedly threatened two teenagers with a gun. The incident happened in Salem. The man, Edward West, 59, is accused of pulling a gun on the teens and saying, "get ready to die." At that moment, a man on a green motorcycle arrived and used his helmet to knock the gun from the man’s hand. This allowed the teens to run away to safety. Police want to find the motorcyclist to thank him.

Tim Sherwood is telling Ron Vlaar to show he still deserves to be Aston Villa’s captain as Vlaar returns from injury. Sherwood wants Vlaar to help the team finish strong in the season, especially since Villa are struggling to avoid relegation. He also warned Vlaar that people might have forgotten his strong performances in the 2014 World Cup, when he played a key role in Holland’s run to the semi-finals — even though he missed a penalty in the shoot-out against Argentina. That performance made him a target for Manchester United. Vlaar, the club’s captain, will return to play as Villa travel to Old Trafford on Saturday. He will play a big role in their fight to stay in the Premier League.

Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about Aston Villa’s possible summer takeover. He plans to build a team that fits his style next season, as long as the club stays in the league. Randy Lerner is reportedly talking to a possible buyer. If a new owner takes over, questions may arise about Sherwood’s job. But Sherwood is only focused on helping the team avoid relegation. After that, he will work on long-term plans during the summer break. The manager says he is not concerned about the takeover talks. Christian Benteke scored and celebrated as Aston Villa beat Sunderland last month.

Celtic have long wanted Manchester City to let Jason Denayer return on loan to Parkhead next season. But things don’t always go as planned. On Thursday, Manchester City’s manager, Manuel Pellegrini, said the club’s young Academy players aren’t ready to play in the first team yet. This means players like Denayer might have to come back early from loan deals to help out. Denayer has done well during his loan spell at Celtic this season.

Southampton's manager, Ronald Koeman, is waiting for a clearer date for Fraser Forster's return before deciding if he needs to sign another goalkeeper in the summer. Forster had knee surgery after falling badly during Southampton's 2-0 win over Burnley two weeks ago. Doctors have given different estimates for his return, ranging from four to 12 months. Koeman doesn’t want to give a more exact date. He thinks Kelvin Davis is a good backup, but says he might have to add another goalkeeper if Forster’s recovery takes longer than expected. Forster got a serious knee injury during the game against Burnley.

Rotherham manager Steve Evans was angry on the touchline after his team, fighting to avoid relegation, were not given a penalty in their close Sky Bet Championship loss at Birmingham. Birmingham had taken the lead in the first half with goals from Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Matt Derbyshire scored for Rotherham, who were fourth from bottom. Later, Rob Kiernan handled the ball near the box, causing Derbyshire to fall. The referee, Dean Whitestone, did not give a penalty, which made Evans very upset. Birmingham then held on to win. Robert Tesche, who scored Birmingham’s first goal, celebrated after scoring.

Virgil van Dijk is worried. The Netherlands national team has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifiers than they did in the whole previous World Cup qualifying campaign. Still, manager Guus Hiddink has not contacted him by phone or letter. Van Dijk was in two national team squads last year, but after one step forward, he usually takes two steps back. When the Dutch drew 1-1 with Turkey, he was relaxing in the Arabian Gulf, hanging out with teammates instead of playing. He has been playing well for Celtic, but still wasn’t called up to the Netherlands national team.

Celtic have complained to the SFA about the ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness, which will be played at Hampden later this month. The match is scheduled for 12:15pm on Sunday, April 18. This time has upset Inverness fans because it’s before the first train from Inverness arrives in Glasgow. Adult tickets are priced at £23 for the North and South stands, and £15 for the East Stand. Concession tickets for the East Stand are £5. Celtic have raised concerns about these prices.

Rangers' interim chairman, Paul Murray, said on Thursday that only the actions of past board members caused the club to be removed from the stock exchange. The team must leave the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) because they couldn’t find a new nominated advisor (Nomad), which is required by law. Murray says the new board’s future plans won’t change and that planned investments will still happen. He also repeated that only past board decisions were to blame for the club’s removal from the stock exchange.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were disappointed with how poorly they started their match against Italy on Tuesday night. It was their second game against Italy in nine months, this time in Turin at the Juventus Stadium. England had won seven games in a row, so expectations were high. But in the first half, Roy Hodgson’s team played badly and fell behind when Graziano Pelle scored with a header. England ended the game with a 1-1 draw. Rooney said he and the other England players were upset by their first-half performance.

Dundee United have responded to strong criticism from two major supporters' groups. Arabtrust and the Federation of Dundee United Supporters Clubs said they were shocked that 25% of the £6.3 million paid for players like Ryan Gauld, Andrew Robertson, Stuart Armstrong, and Gary Mackay-Steven went to unnamed third parties as commission. The groups also questioned how much chairman Stephen Thompson has really invested in the club. In reply, the Dundee United board said their success on the pitch shows their work is effective.

Gary Locke will be officially named Kilmarnock’s permanent manager on Friday, eight weeks after being asked to take charge until the end of the season. The club will make the announcement on Friday morning, and Locke will sign a three-year contract. The 39-year-old, who previously managed Hearts, thanked the players for their hard work, which helped him gain the support of new chairman Jim Mann since he took over as caretaker manager in February. Kilmarnock will confirm Gary Locke as their new permanent manager on Friday.

Chinese parents often want to raise child prodigies—like 10-year-olds who go to university or four-year-olds who copy Michael Jackson’s dance moves. Now, a new young star is growing in popularity. A video is spreading quickly in China showing a small boy with amazing basketball skills, even better than many pro players. The boy is five years old and named Mai Zizhuo. He has been playing basketball since he was two and a half, according to People's Daily Online. The video begins with him making several baskets in a row, then running while dribbling two basketballs at the same time.

Bayern Munich will miss versatile left-back David Alaba for the last part of the season. He has a torn knee ligament and is expected to be out for about seven weeks. Alaba had already been out for three months earlier this season due to a partial ligament tear in his right knee. He got injured during Austria’s 1-1 draw with Bosnia on Tuesday. The 22-year-old said on the club’s website: "I am very disappointed. But I have a big goal — to be back for the final game of the season." Alaba was tackled by Emir Spahic during Austria’s match against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian forward Dane Tilse from the Canberra Raiders to replace Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey, who left the team. Tilse, who is 6ft 7in and weighs over 17 stone, has agreed to a two-and-a-half-year contract with Hull KR. He will join the team as soon as he gets the required paperwork, after the Raiders agreed to release him. Tilse, 30, has played 200 games in Australia. He will play with his old Canberra teammate Terry Campese, who is now Hull KR’s captain and recently signed a two-year contract extension. Tilse is taking over the same role as Weyman, who retired last month because of injury.

Livingston manager Mark Burchill thinks midfielder Darren Cole wants to play in Sunday’s Petrofac Cup final, even though it’s only a week after his cousin, Shaun Cole, died in America. Shaun Cole, 22, was found dead on a Miami street. He had been on holiday in Florida while on leave from the army, where he served in Afghanistan. He had been to a music festival before being found with a head injury that caused his death. The injury is believed to have been caused by a hit-and-run driver. Mark Burchill hopes Darren Cole will play for Livingston on Sunday.

Alan Smith has denied that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance he was in after he was seriously injured during a match against Manchester United nine years ago. The injury happened in February 2006, during the FA Cup fifth round game at Anfield. Smith broke his leg and dislocated his ankle while trying to stop a free-kick by John Arne Riise. At the time, some reports said Liverpool fans threw bottles, beer glasses, and stones at the ambulance and even rocked the vehicle as it drove him to hospital. This content includes graphic images.

Celtic are interested in signing Hearts captain Danny Wilson this summer. They are considering a £400,000 offer for the former Rangers and Liverpool defender. Wilson has one year left on his contract. Hearts owner Ann Budge says the club has no need to sell him, even though he is out of contract at the end of the season. The Edinburgh club, recently promoted, is not in a hurry to sell.

Ronny Deila says Celtic won’t risk their Champions League hopes by doing another long and tough pre-season tour. He says last summer’s series of matches in the United States, Austria, and Germany hurt the team and led to a 4-1 loss in the Champions League qualifier against Legia Warsaw. Celtic earn good money from pre-season games and have played in Australia and the Far East in recent years. Deila and player Nir Bitton left the pitch after the loss to Legia Warsaw. A return to the U.S. this July is still possible, but not confirmed.

Franck Ribery has said that reports linking Wolfsburg player Kevin de Bruyne to a move to Bayern Munich are not true. These reports suggested de Bruyne could replace Ribery or his teammate Arjen Robben. De Bruyne, who was mostly on loan at Chelsea before joining Wolfsburg, has scored nine goals this season and has 16 assists, the most in the Bundesliga. He is seven assists ahead of the next player. But Ribery says that even though de Bruyne is playing well, he is not the right type of player for Bayern under manager Pep Guardiola. Ribery says de Bruyne’s strengths are different from his own and from those of the Dutch winger, Robben.

The girlfriend of an Arizona State University football player who was suspended after she said he abused her has now said she lied. She said her mood swings made her make up the story. Davon Durant, a linebacker at ASU, was arrested on domestic violence charges. His girlfriend, Kelsi Langley, had said he hit her in the face and grabbed her neck during an argument in his car on March 7. After the arrest, Durant— who came to ASU from a Kansas college and was a five-star recruit— was suspended from the football team indefinitely. He could also be expelled.

What could be more exciting than meeting your hero? Meeting your hero at a Starbucks, wearing a shirt with their name on it, and having your photo posted on their Instagram. A young boy got to meet Justin Verlander, a pitcher for the Detroit Tigers, in just those special moments. Verlander took a selfie with the boy, who was wearing a dark blue shirt that had Verlander’s name and his jersey number, 35, on the back. The photo was shared on Verlander’s Instagram.

Eden Hazard said that playing so many games this season with Chelsea might have made him too tired to play his best. He was taken off after 62 minutes in Belgium’s 1-0 win over Israel on Tuesday. Hazard has played 48 games this season for club and country, missing only five matches for Chelsea. He played in every Premier League game as Chelsea fought for the title. But in the match against Israel, he struggled to beat his defender, Orel Dgani, and was substituted with 28 minutes left. Belgium’s manager, Marc Wilmots, made the change.

Drug smugglers were caught when police found marijuana hidden inside a leg of lamb. The meat was discovered in the Northern Territory after a tip led officials to suspect something was wrong. Police x-rayed the lamb and found a 20-gram bag of marijuana inside. The lamb was believed to have been sent to a company at Darwin Airport, and then planned to be delivered to the Tiwi Islands, about 100 kilometers to the north.

Footballer Clarke Carlisle has said he has separated from his wife, Gemma, after struggling with depression following his suicide attempt. He has moved out of their home in Yorkshire, where they lived together for 14 years. Carlisle tried to take his life in December, just two days after being arrested on suspicion of drink-driving.

Arsenal legend Paul Merson had to admit he was wrong after criticizing Andros Townsend's call-up to the England team. Townsend, a Tottenham winger, came on as a substitute and scored a brilliant goal to equalize in England's 1-1 friendly draw against Italy in Turin on Tuesday. This goal was a strong response to Merson's earlier comment in his Sky Sports column, where he said, "If Andros Townsend can get in (the England squad) then it opens it up for anybody." Townsend celebrated his goal with his Tottenham teammates, Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker. The match took place on Tuesday night in Turin.

It's becoming common for Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas to play poorly in the second half of the season. The Spanish player was one of the worst on the field again during Spain's 2-0 loss to Holland on Tuesday. Earlier in the week, the 27-year-old said he was happy living in southwest London. But his performance has dropped a lot since around Christmas, when he seemed certain to break the Barclays Premier League record for assists.

Six people have been arrested in Dover on suspicion of terrorism offences linked to Syria, police said. Five men and one woman were taken into custody around 8am this morning in the departure area of the south coast port. Four of the men, all in their 20s, are from Birmingham in the West Midlands. The other man is 26 years old, and the woman is 23. Neither of them has a fixed address. All six are being questioned at a police station in the West Midlands.

Get ready to buy something — the strongest urge to treat yourself happens today at 12:52pm. A study says people in the UK spend about £62 each week on small rewards. The urge to shop for treats is highest at lunchtime today. Rewards can be simple, like a chocolate bar or a glass of wine, or more expensive, like designer clothes and shoes. This information comes from research by the website VoucherCodes.co.uk. The study also found that men spend about one-third more each month than women on treating themselves.

Arsene Wenger is highly respected and clearly very smart. Sometimes, you agree with something he says, but when you look closer, it sounds true but isn’t really based on strong evidence. This often happens after a bad defensive performance, when he points out that Arsenal’s defensive stats are actually good (which they are). Last week, he spoke about player quotas, especially the idea by FA chairman Greg Dyke to raise the number of homegrown players in a Premier League squad from 8 to 12.

Charlie Austin has said that his friend Joey Barton ignored him on his first day at Queens Park Rangers, not knowing who he was. Later, Barton realized his mistake, and the two became close friends. Austin had a strong first season in the Premier League, scoring 15 goals, and is now being considered for the England national team. Although their friendship is well known, their first meeting is one Austin will never forget.

This dog is definitely his master's best friend after saving him from a cold, muddy grave. The black dog was filmed on Saturday afternoon at the Clarence J. Brown Dam and Reservoir in Springfield, Ohio, pulling a rescue rope to his owner. The man, whose name is not known, was pulled to safety by firefighters after being in water close to zero degrees Celsius for nearly two hours. He had gotten stuck waist-deep in mud while trying to recover some duck hunting gear. He was lucky to have his cell phone and called 911. But firefighters couldn’t send a boat because the river was too shallow.

Juventus coach Massimiliano Allegri says he doesn’t expect the fans to fully accept him until he wins a title with the team. He joined Juventus last summer, after being let go by AC Milan. Since then, he has done well, leading Juventus to a strong lead in the Serie A championship race. Allegri took over from Antonio Conte last summer. On Saturday, Juventus will play at home against Empoli and aim for three more points. Juventus are currently first in Serie A, and Allegri is coaching them from the touchline.

When the game was close, it only took a short time for the key moment to happen. Nathan Redmond had just started playing—only six minutes in—when he made a big difference in this tough match. Steven Whittaker saw the chance and passed the ball to Redmond down the right side, keeping it close to the touchline. Redmond quickly sped past Joe Bennett, and his low pass found Bradley Johnson, who scored at the back post. Johnson celebrated after scoring the winning goal in the second half at the Amex Stadium.

For people in Celoron, New York, the statue of local hero Lucile Ball is not funny. It has upset them for six years. In 2009, the town put up a statue of Ball. But many people said her face looked nothing like her. They were shocked and upset. The statue looks so bad that a Facebook group called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue" got over 600 likes. The statue is based on a scene from her show, "I Love Lucy," where she pretends to sell a health drink while acting drunk.

South Sydney hooker Issac Luke is facing a homophobic accusation after posting a rude comment on social media. The comment came in response to abuse from fans of the Canterbury Bulldogs. The 27-year-old had posted on his official Instagram account on Saturday, asking for help to find a young Rabbitohs fan who was allegedly attacked at ANZ Stadium in Sydney. Luke wanted to give the boy a jersey as a kind gesture, ahead of the Easter long weekend, to make up for the incident that left the boy in hospital after a heated match.

People who fear spiders should be careful — this might scare you. A man in Victoria was shocked when a large huntsman spider crawled out from inside his car door handle. The video, filmed in Wangaratta in northeast Victoria, shows the man walking up to his black Holden Ute and spraying insect repellent on the door. The spray made the spider come out from under the handle. He calmly says, “Get out, you bastard.” But when the spider’s hairy legs suddenly appear, he screams and jumps back in fear.

Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino says Harry Kane is like the former striker Gabriel Batistuta. He also said he will support Kane if things don’t go well. Kane scored just 79 seconds after coming on in his full international debut against Lithuania at Wembley last Friday. That goal put him two away from 30 for the season. England manager Roy Hodgson is careful not to put too much pressure on Kane, who has risen quickly since finally joining Tottenham’s first team after loan spells at Leicester and Norwich. Pochettino still believes Kane is similar to Gabriel Batistuta.

A former footballer who ran a £30 million investment scheme and lived like a millionaire is now surviving on handouts, a court has heard. Michael McIndoe, who played for Bristol City and Wolverhampton Wanderers, convinced other footballers to join the scheme by promising a 20% return. The scheme failed due to growing debts, and in October last year, McIndoe was declared bankrupt with over £2 million in debt. Once known as 'Mr Big' in Marbella, where he socialized with wealthy and attractive people, he is now being pursued by creditors in court.

Juventus director Pavel Nedved said Barcelona are interested in signing Paul Pogba. In an interview with Mundo Deportivo, the former Juventus player — who played 324 games for the club — said Pogba will not be leaving. Nedved also said he was happy Juventus did not face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals. The Czech player, now a director at Juventus, confirmed Pogba will stay at the club.

A man who has a criminal record for sex offenses was reportedly run over by his girlfriend after she said she caught him abusing a 12-year-old girl. James Oliver, 48, suffered a serious leg injury when he was hit by a car driven by Linda Currier, 53. Police found Oliver in the driveway of a house in Noblesboro, Maine, on Saturday night, according to NBC News. Authorities said the two had argued inside the house after Currier saw Oliver allegedly trying to sexually assault the girl.

Liverpool are interested in signing 25-year-old goalkeeper Neto, who plays for Fiorentina. His contract ends in June, and he is also wanted by PSG and clubs in Spain. Brendan Rodgers faces strong competition to sign him, according to Neto’s agent, Stefano Castagna. Liverpool were linked with Neto earlier in the season when Simon Mignolet was left out of the team. A move in January did not happen, but Neto is expected to leave Fiorentina in the summer. He can be seen running from his goal during a match against Roma in March, as Juan Iturbe approached.

Not everyone should drive a $50,000 car. That’s the message from a video posted by YouTube user Richard Stewart. It shows a Porsche Cayman losing control right after a green light in Prince Edward Island, Canada. The car swings sharply from side to side before hitting a concrete barrier. One wheel flies off before the car stops. Stewart wrote on YouTube: "Just because you have a nice car doesn’t mean you’re a good driver. Don’t let your son drive your Porsche!"

Before this weekend's Premier League games, Sportsmail will give you all the key details for each match, including team updates, player lists, betting odds, and stats. Here is what you need to know for the Sunderland game against Newcastle at the Stadium of Light.

Sunderland vs Newcastle United  
Team news:  
Sunderland's midfielder Lee Cattermole will play in the starting line-up for Sunday's derby against Newcastle. Manager Dick Advocaat confirmed that Cattermole is back after serving a two-match ban. He missed two games because he reached 10 yellow cards this season.

If Rory McIlroy wins the upcoming Masters, he will complete a career grand slam, which has been his lifelong goal. As part of his partnership with sponsor Bose, he has released a video showing his journey from playing golf on the back greens as a child to becoming the world’s top golfer, including some tough moments along the way. The video starts with McIlroy jogging early in the morning, with the words "Six weeks to Georgia" on screen. It also includes an interview with a young Rory McIlroy, before he became a famous golfer.

Sergio Garcia says he is focused on winning his first PGA Tour title since 2012 at this week’s Shell Houston Open, even though the Masters is coming up soon. Rory McIlroy’s chance to win his third major in a row and complete a career grand slam, and whether Tiger Woods will return to golf, have been the main topics for weeks. But even though the Golf Club of Houston has been set up to copy some of the conditions at Augusta, Garcia is only thinking about ending his long winless streak. Sergio Garcia was putting during the Cadillac Championship in Doral, Florida, last month.

Riki Hughes, a 31-year-old Iraq war veteran, has been jailed for 16 months after stealing £17,000 from Tidworth Town Football Club. He volunteered as the club’s secretary. He lied about using the money to pay rent, even though the club was getting its property for free. Instead, he spent the money on things like camping gear and a stag trip to Las Vegas. The case was heard at Salisbury Crown Court.

Johnny Sexton is used to success. Winning big trophies has become a regular part of his life, and he is determined to keep it that way. As he got ready for a European Champions Cup quarter-final game against Saracens in Paris, the Racing Metro player and Irish star looked back on his winning ways. He said, "I’ve been very lucky to play with great teams at Leinster and Ireland. Most years, I’ve been part of a team that won a trophy." In fact, since he started playing at the senior level in 2010, the only year he didn’t win a major prize was 2010 itself.

Mustafa Kamal stepped down as ICC president on Wednesday. He said India influenced the result of the Cricket World Cup quarter-final between Bangladesh and India. He made this statement at the airport when he returned from the tournament in Australia. Kamal, who is from Bangladesh, said everyone saw what happened in the Bangladesh-India match. He accused India of using its position in the ICC to affect the game's outcome. He also said he would have reacted the same way if any other country had been treated this way. Mustafa Kamal, who was pictured with the Cricket World Cup trophy, is now a former ICC president.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says he supports Nigel Pearson and respects him for being true to himself. Allardyce worked with Pearson when he was manager of Newcastle United in 2007. The two will meet again when West Ham plays Leicester City at the King Power Stadium on Saturday. Pearson has been in the news for several controversial moments this season, including grabbing Crystal Palace’s James McArthur by the throat and losing his temper during a press conference. Nigel Pearson, who is Leicester City’s manager, has been involved in a number of controversial incidents this season.

Skipper John O'Shea is telling Sunderland to take control of their own fate by winning their fifth straight derby against Newcastle. The match takes place on Sunday at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland have won the last four meetings, but they badly need three points to stay clear of the fight to avoid relegation from the Premier League. If Burnley beat Tottenham earlier in the day, Sunderland could end up in the relegation zone by kick-off. That means winning the game is now essential.

Stoke manager Mark Hughes says it's time for the club to stop losing at Chelsea's home ground, Stamford Bridge. Since Stoke got promoted to the Premier League in 2008, they have played Chelsea away in eight games across all competitions and lost every time. Their last win at Stamford Bridge was in 1995, in a League Cup match. The last time they drew there was in 1984. Stoke's most recent visit ended in a 3-0 loss to Chelsea. Frank Lampard celebrated that win.

Newcastle is hoping to avoid a third straight loss when they play their local rivals Sunderland in Sunday’s important derby game. They have been struggling lately, especially since their top striker, Papiss Cisse, was banned. Newcastle is now at the bottom of the Barclays Premier League, just one point above the teams in the relegation zone. But if it weren’t for Cisse’s goals, Newcastle would be two points worse off and in the relegation zone. Cisse is Newcastle’s top scorer this season with 11 goals, and 10 of those goals have been key in helping the team win games.

Dick Advocaat is bringing back Lee Cattermole, who plays as a central defender, to the middle of his Sunderland team. He hopes this will help the team win their fifth straight derby game in a row, which would be a record. Cattermole, 27, missed the last two games because he got 10 yellow cards this season, which led to a suspension. He also couldn’t play in Advocaat’s first game as manager, a 1-0 loss at West Ham on March 21. But during Friday’s team meeting, Cattermole was the only player told he will definitely start in Sunday’s game against Newcastle.
