For Ronny Deila, making it to the Champions League isn’t just about money. But now there are 16 million reasons for the Norwegian manager to get Celtic there again by winning their fourth straight title. And all of those reasons are about money. This week, UEFA announced the new payment system for European football over the next three years. The last time Celtic played in the Champions League group stage, in 2013-14, they beat only one team (AC Milan) and earned £12.6 million. If they do as well or better next season, that amount would go up by £4 million. If they reach the last 16, they would earn more than £20 million. And that’s not even counting money from ticket sales.

Tottenham defender Ben Davies says he won’t let personal feelings get in the way when he plays against his Wales teammate Sam Vokes at Burnley on Sunday. Tottenham are going to Turf Moor hoping to keep up a good run. They’ve only lost one game in four Premier League matches — at Manchester United — before the international break. They still want to have a chance at qualifying for European football. Burnley are fighting to avoid relegation. They are currently 18th in the league, just one point above the bottom three. Sam Vokes scored against Tottenham in the FA Cup earlier this season, and he celebrated after Burnley equalised in the third round at Turf Moor. At that time, Ben Davies turned away after the goal.

Neil Redfearn is thinking about his job as manager of Leeds United after the club suspended his assistant, Steve Thompson, on Thursday. Leeds took two months to hire Thompson, but on Thursday morning, he received a letter from director of football Nicola Salerno saying he would be suspended until the end of the season. This means he will not continue at the club after 105 days. He has also been told that the club will not use an option to renew his contract. Steve Thompson, the assistant manager, has been suspended by Leeds United.

John Carver says he might use a whip to motivate his Newcastle players before Sunday’s Tyne-Wear derby at the Stadium of Light. Newcastle has lost the last four games against Sunderland. Carver, who was assistant to Alan Pardew during those losses, admits Sunderland wanted to win more than Newcastle did in those matches. “In the last four games, Sunderland worked harder than us – and that’s not a good record,” he said. Carver says he will ‘whip’ his players to make sure they are ready and determined to beat Sunderland on Sunday.

David Templeton has strongly criticized the training methods used at Rangers under managers Ally McCoist and Kenny McDowall. The Rangers winger said Stuart McCall brought a new style of coaching and tactical planning that he felt was missing under the previous management. Templeton praised McCall’s impact since he joined on a short-term deal last month. Two consecutive wins have boosted team confidence ahead of Saturday’s home game against Hearts, who won the Championship title. Rangers winger David Templeton is very positive about the change McCall has made.

Nolito, a forward for Celta Vigo, says Lionel Messi should not play in their La Liga game on Sunday. Messi has a foot injury but has been training and is expected to be fit. Nolito, 28, says he hopes Messi stays home and spends the day at the beach instead. He joked that he might call Messi’s dad. Messi is expected to play for Barcelona against Celta Vigo after recovering from the injury. Barcelona’s forward trained with teammate Javier Mascherano on Thursday.

Robbie Neilson says that players like captain Danny Wilson will only leave Hearts if he believes it’s the right decision for the club. As Sportsmail reported this week, Celtic are interested in signing Wilson, who used to play for Rangers. Before Sunday’s Championship game against Rangers, Neilson said it’s natural that other clubs will want his promoted players. The Hearts manager says he won’t sell any players unless it’s the right move for the team. He agrees with owner Ann Budge that any departures must be approved by him, and only if the price is right.

Sam Allardyce has told Brendan Rodgers that giving Raheem Sterling a big new contract could cause problems with the rest of the Liverpool team. Allardyce thinks that if Sterling gets paid more than the £100,000 a week he was already offered, his teammates might demand higher pay too. But Allardyce doesn’t blame Sterling, who earns £35,000 a week at Liverpool, for wanting the most he can get. He says there are not many young players with real talent, so clubs are paying very high wages to get any good young players they can. Raheem Sterling, a Liverpool and England player, has not yet signed a new contract with Liverpool.

Blackpool are discussing signing Austria defender Thomas Piermayr, who is 25. He has been training with the Championship club this week. Blackpool want to sign him ahead of what is expected to be a League One season next year. Piermayr is a free agent and previously played for Colorado Rapids. He once played for Inverness Caledonian Thistle in 2011. He has never played in England before, but Blackpool could give him his first chance there.

Tony Pulis wants to talk with West Bromwich Albion chairman Jeremy Peace after the team is safe in the Premier League. His goal is to help the club return to the top ten. Pulis said the team has not been doing well in recent years and needs big changes to improve. West Brom finished 10th and 8th under managers Roy Hodgson and Steve Clarke. Last season, they had a tough time and barely avoided relegation, finishing 17th. Tony Pulis, the team's manager, is seen shouting instructions from the sideline during a match against Manchester City.

Arsenal legend Ian Wright says he would be sad if Theo Walcott left the club. He thinks Walcott has struggled because Arsene Wenger hasn't played him as a striker. Walcott has only started five games this season since coming back from a serious knee injury that kept him out for seven months. With Arsenal looking to sign Raheem Sterling and Walcott's contract ending next summer, Wright is worried the team might lose a key player.

Roberto Martinez believes Ross Barkley can become an even more important player for Everton and England after overcoming his second-season slump at Goodison Park. Barkley has had a mixed season with Everton, following his selection for England’s World Cup squad last summer and a knee injury that delayed his return to action. Despite this, England manager Roy Hodgson has continued to trust the 21-year-old. Martinez says Barkley’s two substitute appearances for England in recent games against Lithuania and Italy show he is ready to improve again.

England will not take part in the Under 19 European Championships this summer. They lost 2-1 to France in their final qualifying match. England had won their first two matches in the Elite Round, against Denmark and Azerbaijan. To qualify, they needed to beat France in Saint-Lo. France scored through Sehrou Guirassy and Gnaly Cornet, taking the lead. Fulham player Patrick Roberts scored late for England, but it was not enough. The team, managed by Sean O'Driscoll, failed to reach the finals in Greece.

Newcastle midfielder Jonas Gutierrez wants to mark his return to the first team with a win in the derby against struggling Sunderland. The 31-year-old Argentine has come on as a substitute in each of the last three games since recovering from testicular cancer. He has been warmly welcomed back by teammates and fans. But he has lost each time. Now he is determined to end that losing streak. Newcastle are trying to recover after suffering four straight defeats to Sunderland at the Stadium of Light. The match is on Sunday.

After a close game between South Sydney and Canterbury ended in controversy, NRL referees and officials were hit with thrown objects by angry fans. The Rabbitohs won 18-17 in the final minute at ANZ Stadium in Sydney during a Good Friday match. The decision to penalize Bulldogs captain James Graham in the final minute led to the fans turning on referee Gerard Sutton and his team. As the referees, officials, and players walked off the field and toward the tunnel after the game, some fans threw plastic water bottles and shouted insults at them.

Kevin Sinfield, who is 34 and was the captain of Leeds Rhinos, has said he will leave rugby league at the end of the season. He will join Yorkshire Carnegie, the sister club of Leeds Rhinos, on an 18-month contract. This move to rugby union has surprised many in the rugby league world. Sinfield, who is considered the greatest captain in Leeds' history, has been told he may become a target in his new sport.

Raheem Sterling says he isn't ready to sign a new contract at Liverpool, even though he was offered £100,000 a week to stay. The 20-year-old winger said in a BBC interview that a year ago he would have accepted a much lower pay deal. Although he is one of Liverpool’s top players, Sterling hasn’t played as well this season as he did last year. He has scored only six goals this season—just one more than Stoke’s Jon Walters—and his ability to score goals and his performance per minute have gotten worse, as shown in the chart below.

Brighton and Hove Albion are teaching their young players about the law and ethics of sexual consent. The club is the first in the Championship to offer this kind of training and counselling. The Protect, Inform and Prevent (PIP) programme helps players understand what legally counts as consent. The training includes private question-and-answer sessions where players can talk about past experiences. These sessions are led by a former police detective and a psychotherapist.

A new video shows homeless people reading mean tweets that were written about them. The video, made by Leo Burnett Toronto for the charity Humans For Humans, is meant to make people think differently about people who sleep on the streets. Many of the people cry while reading messages like, "I hate the homeless, I don’t feel sorry for you," and "I saw a homeless girl across the street. I almost vomited." The video is meant to make viewers feel emotional.

George Boyd is the hardest-working player in the Barclays Premier League this season. He ran 210.5 miles during games, which is the same distance as running from Burnley’s Turf Moor stadium to Crystal Palace’s Selhurst Park in south London. He ran a little farther than Tottenham’s Christian Eriksen. Normally, walking that distance would take 69 hours, according to Google Maps. But Boyd covered it in less than 40 hours of actual playing time. George Boyd is the Barclays Premier League's hardest working player, running 210.5 miles on the pitch.

Police have arrested the parents of a five-month-old baby who died yesterday. The baby’s father, 25, and mother, 25, both from Perry Barr in Birmingham, were taken into custody. Police were called to their home just before 1am yesterday after someone said the baby was having trouble breathing. The baby was taken to Birmingham Children's Hospital but died a few hours later. The house where the baby lived is in Perry Barr, Birmingham. The death is being treated as suspicious. A post mortem exam will be done today to find out exactly what caused the baby’s death.

Raheem Sterling, a 20-year-old England player, is not being disloyal to Liverpool by delaying talks about a new contract until the summer, according to his agent, Gordon Taylor. The club offered Sterling what manager Brendan Rodgers called an "incredible" deal, thought to be £100,000 a week. But talks have not reached an agreement. Sterling says he is not just after money, and Taylor, who is head of the Professional Footballers' Association, thinks waiting until the season ends could be a smart choice. Sterling also said in a TV interview that he is not ready to sign a new contract with Liverpool.

Anderson hasn’t done well since leaving Manchester United to go back to Brazil. But on Wednesday, his mistake was overshadowed by a worse one from a teammate. The Brazilian midfielder was sent off in the first half for pushing Ypiranga Erechim striker Otacilio Neto, even though it was off the ball. Otacilio also got sent off for hitting back with an elbow. However, Anderson was lucky because his teammate Fabricio got a red card too for swearing at their own fans. That made Internacional play with only seven players left. The game ended in a 1-1 draw in Porto Alegre.

A seven-year-old boy was raped and set on fire by two teenage boys after he went to buy food. The two youths took him to a remote area and raped him. When he tried to fight back, they set him on fire, according to Inspector Sasthe, who spoke to PTI. The boy, who had burns covering 30% of his body, managed to escape. The incident happened in Padma Nagar, part of Bhiwandi City, a suburb of Mumbai. Police are now investigating the case.

A pug named Dug has made a surprising recovery after being bitten in the face by a rattlesnake. Dug and his owner, Lindsay Castro, were hiking on the Jurupa Hills trail in Fontana, Canada, on Thursday when they heard a rattling sound. Lindsay stepped back, but Dug ran toward the sound and was bitten. The snake bit him on the face, and his face quickly swelled to twice its normal size.

Jose Mourinho might one day return to manage Real Madrid, even after leaving in a difficult way, according to Real Madrid defender Alvaro Arbeloa. Mourinho left Real Madrid after three years in 2013 to go back to Chelsea. He left under tense circumstances, with reports of arguments with key players like Iker Casillas, Sergio Ramos, and Pepe. But Arbeloa, who has played 25 times for Real this season, says the club would always be open to bringing Mourinho back as manager. Arbeloa says Mourinho could still take charge of Real Madrid one day.

Liverpool and their manager Brendan Rodgers ended a difficult period at the Emirates on Saturday. Their chance to qualify for the Champions League is now over. In a 15-minute press conference, Rodgers admitted the team no longer has a realistic shot. He tried to stay positive, as he always does, but he did not hide that this has been a tough season. After coming close to winning the title last year, Liverpool are now out of the race. For a club that had hoped to return to greatness, this is a hard blow. Still, the team seems to be making progress under Rodgers.

Inter Milan coach Roberto Mancini canceled his players' day off on Easter Sunday and made them train early in the morning after a 1-1 draw with Parma, who were at the bottom of the league. The first team trained at 8:30 a.m. local time. Club vice-president Javier Zanetti and sporting director Piero Ausilio were at the training session. Mancini was angry with his players' performance. The draw left Inter in ninth place, level with Genoa, 10 points behind the teams that qualify for European competition.

Many fans want to own a special item that once belonged to their favorite player or team. Small pieces of sports history can sell for thousands of pounds. But it might surprise you that an old passport belonging to Paul Parker — best known for playing as a right back for Manchester United and England in the 1990s — was listed on eBay for £5,000. The listing was made earlier in March, and bidding ended on Tuesday. It is not clear if anyone actually paid that amount. Paul Parker, a former Manchester United and England defender, once used this passport.

He has been seen on toast, pancakes, crisps, and even ice cream. But a builder was shocked when he found a picture of Jesus Christ on a piece of wood just a few days before Easter. Paddy Morrall saw the full-size image of Jesus on a broken scaffolding board in Inverness, Scotland, on Wednesday. The board had been left out in the rain for several hours. Jesus was shown wearing a robe. Paddy Morrall, a 31-year-old builder from Keighley, near Bradford, has kept the board.

Ondrej Duda scored in the second half to help Slovakia beat the Czech Republic 1-0 in a friendly match on Tuesday. The 20-year-old midfielder scored with a low shot from outside the penalty area in the 49th minute. It was his second goal for Slovakia. This was the third time Slovakia has won in their last 10 matches against the Czechs since the two countries split from Czechoslovakia in 1993. The Czechs have won five of those games. During the match, Martin Skrtel kicked Daniel Kolar in the face with a high boot. Slovakia players celebrated their 1-0 win, which continues their strong recent performance.

Karim Benzema showed he can do more than just play football. While preparing for Real Madrid’s La Liga game against Granada on Sunday, he shared a video of himself rapping along to Tupac’s song "Check Out Time" in his Bugatti Veyron. The song "All Eyez on Me" might have been a better fit for him, since he’s aiming to score more goals. So far this season, Benzema has scored 20 goals in all competitions. The Real Madrid and France player is known for his football skills, but now fans have seen his talent in music too.

A wealthy businessman who supports UKIP, Harvey Boulter, is trying to stop a popular Conservative candidate from winning an election. Boulter previously helped force Liam Fox to resign as Defence Secretary. He has already given £30,000 to the UKIP candidate running against Fox in Somerset. He is also spending another £30,000 to try to defeat Tom Tugendhat, who is the Conservative candidate in Tonbridge and West Malling, Kent. This is part of a continuing effort to oppose Fox.

In a Yorkshire derby, Sheffield Wednesday and Huddersfield drew 1-1. Sheffield Wednesday's substitute, Sergiu Bus, scored in the 86th minute. Just one minute before the game ended, Huddersfield's substitute, Ishmael Miller, scored to equalize. This result means Huddersfield has not won in their last seven games. They are now 18th in the league, nine points and six places behind Sheffield Wednesday. Sergiu Bus celebrated after scoring to put Sheffield Wednesday ahead against Huddersfield.

Stuart Dallas has made big progress since Mark Warburton found him playing part-time on a muddy field for Crusaders in Northern Ireland for £70 a week. The 23-year-old, who played well for Northern Ireland earlier in the week, scored two great goals as Brentford beat Fulham 4-1 on Good Friday. The win puts Brentford in a strong position ahead of their match against Nottingham Forest on Monday, with hopes of more than just a play-off spot. It was three years ago that Warburton first saw Dallas play. Dallas celebrated his second goal against Fulham on Good Friday. He has been a standout player this season, helping Brentford move closer to the Premier League.

Baseball is often seen as America's favorite sport, so it's not surprising that people feel strongly about their favorite professional team. The New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox are the two most famous and historic teams. They are the top two in popularity, with the Yankees ranked first and the Red Sox second when it comes to fans who say they are their favorite. The Texas Rangers and Atlanta Braves also have many fans, especially in the southern United States. Some teams, like the New York Mets, are less popular and don’t have as many fans.

A high school basketball star has won hearts by asking a girl with Down syndrome to the prom. Trey Moses, a senior at Eastern High School in Louisville, Kentucky, who will play college basketball at Ball State next year, asked Ellie Meredith to be his date. Trey, who volunteers with teens who have learning disabilities, surprised Ellie during her P.E. class. He gave her flowers and a sign that said, "Let's Party Like it's 1989," a nod to a Taylor Swift album that Ellie loves. Ellie said yes and shared that she’s excited to go dress shopping, saying, "I’ve only told about a million people!" she told CNN.

On April Fools' Day, President Barack Obama joked around by pretending to be the fictional president Frank Underwood from the TV show *House of Cards*. He said, "Hello everybody. This is not Frank Underwood," then added, "This is Barack Obama. Happy April Fools' Day. Frank learned it from me." The character Frank Underwood is played by actor Kevin Spacey, who won an Oscar. Underwood often speaks in a dramatic, Shakespeare-like way to the audience. In the joke, Obama used a southern accent to sound like the character.

Caykur Rizespor midfielder Ludovic Obraniak was taken to hospital on Saturday after he was substituted during a match against Fenerbahce. He had to leave the game after only 30 minutes because of a possible heart problem. He was sent for medical tests. The club said on social media that preliminary tests showed he was not in immediate danger. Obraniak, a Polish player, is on loan from Werder Bremen in Germany. Moussa Sow scored for Fenerbahce during their 5-1 win on Saturday.

Three people were taken to hospital after a head-on crash between a vintage sports car and a 4WD. The accident happened on Easter Sunday night at a traffic light on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney. The 1973 E-Type Jaguar, worth more than $120,000, was completely destroyed in the crash. It hit a Toyota Kluger during a Sunday drive. No one was hurt in the crash, but all three adults were taken to hospital as a safety measure. NSW police are still looking into what caused the crash.

People in Lijin village, Dongying city, Shandong Province, China, have been seen carrying natural gas in large plastic bags. Some bags are as long as six meters. They transport the gas on rickshaws. The gas is dangerous and can explode if it comes into contact with fire or a cigarette. Many people are worried because it looks like carrying a bomb. Local media say this practice helps villages save money on gas transport.

Tiger Woods has been seen practicing on the driving range at Augusta National, which has raised hopes he might play in this year’s Masters, the first major of the season. He hasn’t played on the PGA Tour since pulling out of the Farmers Insurance Open on February 5 due to a return of his back injury. Since then, he has taken time off to recover and get back to his best. There has been talk that he might come back for the Masters, a tournament he has won four times. He was seen practicing at Augusta on Tuesday and has returned to the course. This year, he has also dropped out of the top 100 in the world rankings for the first time in nearly 19 years.

The BBC has been criticized for spending thousands of pounds of licence fee money on a 44-page guide that teaches its staff how to use emojis correctly. The guide was created after BBC bosses asked an agency to study how smiley faces could be used in news stories and on social media. The BBC also paid for emoji designs of famous people like Gary Lineker and Graham Norton. Despite spending money on this guide, the BBC later used a 'sad face' emoji to describe the death of the world’s oldest woman.

One of the world’s top long-distance runners and a frequent training partner of Mo Farah says he is afraid for his life. He says he reported to Ugandan authorities that a coach has been sexually abusing female runners, some as young as 15. Moses Kipsiro, who won the 10,000m title at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow last year, told Sportsmail that five female runners came to him for help on one day. He also said he has received death threats since reporting the abuse to his national sports federation and the police.

Patrick Kluivert, a former Dutch footballer and assistant coach, has started his time as Curacao’s coach with a win in the 2018 World Cup qualifiers. Curacao, a team from the Caribbean island, moved on to the second round of CONCACAF qualifying. They drew 2-2 in their second-leg game in Montserrat, winning 4-3 on aggregate. Curacao had previously won 2-1 on Saturday in Willemstad. Kluivert, who once worked with Louis van Gaal during the 2014 World Cup as Holland’s assistant, helped lead Curacao to this success.

An 18-year-old student who was caught on video biting the head off a live hamster has been kicked out of his fraternity, stopped attending college, and sent for a mental health evaluation. Last weekend, DailyMail.com revealed that Brady Eaves, a student from a private school and the stepson of a former Mississippi governor candidate, was the teen who laughed while killing the small animal at a drunken Spring Break party in Florida. The video could lead to felony animal cruelty charges against Eaves, which could result in up to five years in jail and a fine of $5,000.

Sri Lanka's sports minister, Navin Dissanayake, said Kumar Sangakkara should think again about retiring from limited-overs cricket and play for one more year. Sangakkara retired from one-day cricket on March 18, after the team lost in the World Cup quarter-final. He said he was happy that Sri Lanka is in better shape now than when he joined in 2000. The minister told reporters that he respectfully asks Sangakkara to serve the country for another year. This came after the minister named a new temporary group to run cricket, led by former test cricketer Sidath Wettimuny.

Edinburgh are bringing back three Scotland players for Sunday’s European Challenge Cup quarter-final against London Irish. Dougie Fife, Alasdair Dickinson, and Ross Ford missed last week’s Pro12 match against Scarlets because they had played in the Six Nations. They have now been selected again by head coach Alan Solomons for the game at the Madejski Stadium. The South African coach wants to field his strongest team. Dougie Fife is one of three Scottish players returning to Edinburgh after the Six Nations. In a separate image, England’s Courtney Lawes is tackled by Scotland’s Ross Ford and David Denton.

Chris Ramsey says Tony Pulis is one of the best British managers, but he doesn’t need advice from him on tactics. Ramsey’s QPR play West Brom, managed by Pulis, at the Hawthorns on Saturday. QPR are 19th in the Premier League, four points behind Sunderland in 17th. Since the start of the year, QPR have only earned four points. They need a strong finish like Pulis’s 2013-14 season with Crystal Palace, when his team got 17 points from their last eight games to avoid relegation. Ramsey spoke highly of Pulis ahead of the important match against West Brom.

An 18-year-old teenage girl, Silhan Ozcelik, has appeared in court. She is accused of planning to travel abroad to join Kurdish rebels fighting against the Islamic State. She went missing from her family home in north London in October when she was 17. The court heard that she traveled on the Eurostar train with another man to Stuttgart, Germany. This city is where the youth branch of the Kurdish Workers’ Party (PKK) is based. Silhan Ozcelik, who is in her sixth form, is also accused of preparing to carry out a terrorist attack in October 2014.

Leicester City midfielder Esteban Cambiasso knows what it's like to win football's biggest trophies. But he says saving Leicester from relegation would be one of the best moments of his career. Cambiasso, who played for Argentina, won five Serie A titles with Inter Milan and also won the Champions League in 2010. He told the BBC on Thursday that avoiding relegation would feel like winning a trophy. He joined Leicester last summer on a free transfer and signed a one-year contract at the King Power Stadium.

Crystal Palace manager Alan Pardew says Manchester City still have a chance to win the Barclays Premier League title, even though Chelsea are six points ahead with one game left. Last season, City came from behind to beat Liverpool and win the title, and in 2012, Sergio Aguero scored in stoppage time to beat Manchester United and win the title on goal difference. Pardew, whose team plays City on Monday, says the title race is not over yet. He also noted that he once cupped his ears during a match against Stoke, but that doesn’t change his view that City can still win.

Hull City has asked the Football Association again to change the club's name to Hull Tigers, after the first request was denied. This upset fans who thought the club would keep its current name, since the FA council voted against the change 47 to 27. But now, Hull manager Steve Bruce has said the club has made another application to the FA to rebrand as Hull Tigers. If club owner Assem Allam gets his way, Hull City will become Hull Tigers. Allam still wants the name change, even though fans are angry. An arbitration panel has decided that Allam can make another request to change the name.

A man who lost his sight 12 years ago has found a passion for painting and can make striking images just by touching them. John Bramblitt, 42, had epilepsy starting at age 11. Over the next 19 years, it slowly took away his eyesight. By age 30, he was completely blind. Even though he couldn’t see, he chose not to let that stop him from painting. He lives in Denton, Texas. He uses a special method: first, he applies fabric paint to make an outline, then he adds color to finish the piece.

Before Saturday's Premier League game, Sportsmail is giving you all the key details for every match, including team news, player lists, betting odds, and stats. Here’s what you need to know for Chelsea’s home game against Stoke City at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea:  
Chelsea will decide late whether Diego Costa plays against Stoke. He hurt his hamstring in their win at Hull and missed Spain’s international games. Even though he’s now fit after the break, he might not play because the team could be cautious about risking him.

Ibrox has been a tough place for Rangers this season. Three times this season, teams from Edinburgh have visited and beaten Rangers. Hearts beat them 2-1 in August, and Hibernian won 3-1 and 2-0. Rangers' manager Stuart McCall says his team now must win against Hearts on Sunday to make up for the losses. This is their last chance in the regular season. A 2-0 win over Hibernian at Easter Road 12 days ago might have been a turning point, helping Rangers' promotion hopes, which had been struggling before.

If you like complicated stories full of mystery, avoiding the game against Paisley last night made sense. Celtic, who were close to winning the Treble, played against St Mirren, who were struggling and at risk of falling apart. It didn’t seem likely to be an exciting match. But even though Celtic won, the game showed clearly that they won’t easily win their fourth straight title in the coming weeks. Kris Commons, a Celtic winger, tried to score during the SPL game against St Mirren on Friday.

Ulster have signed Charles Piutau, a New Zealand international. Piutau can play as full back, wing, or centre. He has agreed to a two-year contract starting in July 2016. He has played 14 times for the All Blacks and made his Test debut against France two years ago. He has played for the Blues in New Zealand since 2012. Ulster team manager Bryn Cunningham said it is very exciting to get someone with Piutau’s talent.

Alessandro Diamanti and Mohamed Salah helped Fiorentina beat Sampdoria 2-0 in a rainy match. The win moved Fiorentina to fourth place with 49 points. Diamanti scored just after the 60th minute, and Salah scored the second goal two minutes later. In another game, Miralem Pjanic scored the only goal as AS Roma beat Napoli 1-0. It was Roma’s first home win in over four months. Mohamed Salah also continued his good form by scoring again while on loan from Chelsea. After scoring Fiorentina’s second goal, Salah turned away.

Juventus won 2-0 against Empoli on Saturday, moving closer to a fourth straight Serie A title. Carlos Tevez scored just before halftime, and Roberto Pereyra scored again in stoppage time. The win gave Juventus a 14-point lead at the top of the league with nine games left. This puts a fourth straight Serie A title within reach for Juventus. The match was played at Juventus's home ground.

Kevin de Bruyne’s agent has said there is no deal for him to leave Wolfsburg in the summer. However, he admitted that several clubs are watching the Belgian player. De Bruyne has become one of the most sought-after players in Europe after doing well in the Bundesliga. He has been linked with Manchester City and Bayern Munich. Speaking to FOCUS Online, his agent Patrick De Koster said that many clubs are interested, and there has been some informal talk. But no transfer has been agreed.

Swansea manager Garry Monk wants to win against Hull on Saturday to get their first points of the season after the international break. Swansea have had a strong season, staying in the top 10 all year, and are currently in eighth place. They are close to their best ever Barclays Premier League points total. They have eight games left and need five more points to beat the 47-point mark from their first Premier League season in 2011-12. During a training session this week, Monk pointed to his striker, Bafetimbi Gomis.

Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo are known as two of the greatest football rivals today. But former Brazil striker Ronaldo, who won the 2002 World Cup, says he would like them both to play for his team one day. He is a co-owner of Fort Lauderdale Strikers, a second-tier football team in the United States. Ronaldo wants to make his team a top global club. He says he would spend his own money to sign Messi. He also wants Cristiano Ronaldo to join the team.

Northampton will wait for expert advice before deciding when George North will play again. He will miss Saturday’s European Champions Cup quarter-final against Clermont Auvergne because of a head injury. North has been knocked unconscious three times in recent months, including during last Friday’s match against Wasps, which they won 52-30. On Wednesday, he was seen by a neurologist. “We won’t play him at the weekend,” said Saints’ director of rugby, Jim Mallinder. George North was lying still on the grass at Franklin’s Gardens after being knocked out during the Wasps game. “He clearly had a bad hit. He was unconscious for a short time.”

Cesar Azpilicueta is waiting for the final games before Chelsea win the Barclays Premier League. He believes the team has proven they are strong by staying at the top of the league since the first day. Chelsea are currently first in the table, ahead of their match against Stoke City at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. They are six points ahead of second-place Manchester City, and they have one more game to play. Chelsea have been seen as strong title contenders for a while. Azpilicueta says this is because they started the season very well—winning seven of their first eight games—and took the lead early. Cesar Azpilicueta (centre) is counting down the games until Chelsea win the Barclays Premier League title.

Mohamed Diame will return for Hull City when they play Swansea on Saturday. The Senegalese midfielder, who joined Hull for £3.5 million from West Ham in the summer, has been out for over four months with a knee injury. Hull's manager, Steve Bruce, confirmed Diame will play part of the game. Bruce said Diame is physically strong and in good shape, but he has had a tough injury. His return is a big help for Hull, who are fighting to avoid relegation.

Toby Alderweireld will go back to Atletico Madrid when his loan from them ends at Southampton. The Spanish club's sporting director, Jose Luis Perez Caminero, said this. Alderweireld, a 26-year-old Belgian defender, has played well during his time at Southampton. He has previously said he would like to stay in the Premier League, and Tottenham are also interested in him. But Atletico Madrid expect him to return to La Liga, along with Oliver Torres, who is playing in Portugal with Porto.

Tom Carroll, a Swansea midfielder and England Under 21 player, may miss up to six weeks because of ankle ligament damage. He got hurt during England’s 1-0 win over the Czech Republic last Friday. He also scored the only goal in that match, helping England win in Prague. Carroll, who is on loan from Tottenham, has made 18 appearances for Swansea this season. After scoring, he celebrated with his teammates.

Franck Ribery says he won’t be able to play against Borussia Dortmund this week because he hasn’t recovered from his injury. He admits he can’t even run. He limped off during a game against Shakhtar Donetsk at the start of last month. That game also saw Bayern Munich’s other winger, Arjen Robben, get injured. Ribery hopes he might be back in time for the German Cup quarter-final against Bayer Leverkusen later in the week. The photos show Ribery celebrating a Champions League goal against Shakhtar Donetsk and being tackled by Braunschweig’s defender Benjamin Kessel.

Philipp Lahm, Bayern Munich's captain, might play in his first Bundesliga game since coming back from an ankle injury when Bayern face Borussia Dortmund on Saturday. Several key players are out: Franck Ribery (ankle), Arjen Robben (stomach), Javi Martinez (knee), and David Alaba (knee). Coach Pep Guardiola is still unsure if defender Holger Badstuber (hip) will be able to play. Midfielder Thiago Alcantara might play for a few minutes, as he recovers from long-term knee problems. Lahm has fully recovered from his broken ankle. Guardiola will miss several first-team players in the match against Dortmund.

Michael Duff, a long-time Burnley defender, thinks manager Sean Dyche could one day manage the England national team. Dyche, who is 43, has built a strong reputation since he joined Burnley in October 2012. He turned the team around, proving many wrong by leading Burnley from being seen as relegation candidates to winning promotion from the Championship to the Premier League last season. Duff is now preparing to play against Tottenham in the Premier League on Sunday. He still believes Dyche has what it takes to manage England one day.

Mauricio Pochettino has allowed Harry Kane to play in the European Under 21 Championships this summer. Roy Hodgson has confirmed that the Tottenham striker will be in Gareth Southgate's squad for the tournament in the Czech Republic. This is despite Kane making his senior England debut just last week. Kane will also travel to Australia and Malaysia this summer before the championships. He played for England against Italy and will now play for the U21 team in this year’s European Championships. Kane made his first start for England in the game against Italy, after coming on as a substitute and scoring in the match against Lithuania.

Alvaro Morata wants to keep growing at Juventus and does not want to go back to Real Madrid, says his agent, Beppe Bozzo. The 22-year-old moved to Juventus last summer for £15.8 million after not getting enough chances to play regularly for Real Madrid’s first team. He signed a five-year contract with Juventus after starting only three games in La Liga for Real during the 2013-14 season. Morata is happy at Juventus and has no desire to return to Real Madrid, according to his agent. Since joining, he has done well – scoring seven goals in 22 Serie A games this season.

Hundreds of football fans are facing travel problems this weekend because of train closures over Easter. More than 30 top football games are planned, but many train lines will be closed for repairs. Over half of the games will be delayed or disrupted, so fans will have to drive instead. The important match between Arsenal and Liverpool in London will also be affected by the train problems. Labour says the government did not learn from a similar problem on Boxing Day, when almost a million fans had terrible travel experiences.

Brentford manager Mark Warburton was happy after his team won 4-1 against Fulham in a tough west London derby at Craven Cottage. Stuart Dallas scored two goals, Alan Judge scored a great free-kick in the second half, and Jota added a fourth goal late in the game. The win moved Brentford to fifth place in the league with 69 points, with six games left. They are still in the running for a play-off spot. Warburton said he was really pleased with the team's performance.

The Barclays Premier League has announced the last group of matches to be shown on TV for the 2014-15 season. As the season ends, the final TV schedules for Sky Sports and BT Sport have been released, with the battle for Champions League spots being a key part. The most important games are Chelsea vs Liverpool on May 10 and Manchester United vs Arsenal on May 17. The TV schedule for the final day, Sunday, May 24, will be announced later. Juan Mata scored for Manchester United against Liverpool last month in a game shown live on TV. Manchester United also beat Arsenal at the Emirates earlier in the season. Saturday, May 2.

The Quick Silver P-51D Mustang is a U.S. fighter jet that is about 70 years old. It was rebuilt from more than 200 parts by a father-and-son team, Bill and Scooter Yoak. They restored it as a tribute to American soldiers who died in combat. The jet now flies again, and a video from inside the cockpit shows it soaring through the sky. The restoration was done carefully, and the jet looks amazing.

Brazil's World Cup stadium in Natal is for sale because the company that owns it is having money problems after a corruption scandal. The company, Grupo OAS, is selling the Dunas Arena in Natal and also trying to sell its 50% share in the Fonte Nova arena in Salvador. The company has had difficulties for months because of a corruption investigation at Petrobras, the state oil company, which has made it hard for the builder to get loans. A photo shows the Dunas Arena in Natal during a World Cup match between Italy and Uruguay last year.

A group of 13 U.S. senators, both Democrats and Republicans, wrote a letter to FIFA, the world's football governing body. They asked FIFA to remove Russia as host of the 2018 World Cup. The senators said this because of Russia's role in the Ukraine crisis and its occupation of Crimea. The letter, dated Tuesday and released on Wednesday, says they "strongly encourage" FIFA to move the World Cup to another country.

Five people, including Thomaz Alckmin—the son of São Paulo’s governor, Geraldo Alckmin—died when a helicopter crashed into a house in the Carapicuiba area on the outskirts of São Paulo. The crash happened at about 5:20 p.m. local time yesterday. The helicopter hit a residential neighborhood and landed on a house, killing five people. One of the victims was reportedly Thomaz Alckmin.

Jos Hooiveld scored late to give Millwall a vital 2-1 win over Charlton, their local rivals, on Good Friday. It was Millwall’s first win at The Den since October. Gueye’s low shot was blocked, but Hooiveld put it in the net in the 87th minute. Gueye had earlier equalized after Alou Diarra had given Charlton the lead. Charlton’s captain, Chris Solly, was sent off in the first half for deliberately handling the ball in the penalty area. Millwall’s goalkeeper, Stephen Henderson, saved Lee Gregory’s penalty kick. Substitute Magaye Gueye celebrated scoring the equalizer in Millwall’s 2-1 win over Charlton. Charlton defender Chris Solly

The hatchback is the most popular car in the world this year, even though it’s not as fast as a Ferrari or as fancy as a Rolls Royce. It turns 50 years old this year. The design started in the 1960s to help French farmers carry sheep to market. Now, two out of every three cars sold in the UK are hatchbacks. They are also very popular around the world, from Munich to Mexico City, because they are practical, fuel-efficient, and comfortable. The first hatchback ever made was the Renault 16, which was introduced in April 1965. The Renault 4, which came before the Renault 16, was also designed to help French farmers carry sheep.

Venezuela captain Juan Arango has apologized to a rival player after biting him during a heated Mexican league game. Arango was playing for Tijuana, who were losing 4-3 to Monterrey with only seconds left. He bit midfielder Jesus Zavala on the shoulder. The 34-year-old Arango said, "I did something I shouldn't have done with Zavala." The incident happened in a moment of anger. Zavala held his shoulder after being bitten. He showed the referee the mark left by the bite. Monterrey won the game 4-3.

Paul Merson has criticized Andros Townsend again after Townsend played in the final seven minutes of Tottenham’s 0-0 draw with Burnley on Sunday. Merson posted on Twitter: “Just been watching the game, did you miss the coach? #RubberDub #7minutes.” This follows an earlier comment by Merson in a Sky Sports column, where he said that if Townsend can make the England team, then anyone could. Townsend came on in the 83rd minute of the match.

Cristiano Ronaldo is not getting worse — reports of his decline are wrong. The Real Madrid player scored five goals against Granada, bringing his total in La Liga to 36 for the season. That is more than half of the top teams in Europe. Real Madrid won the game 9-1 at the Bernabeu, with Ronaldo and his teammates dominating Granada. This was the first time in his career that Ronaldo scored five goals in one game. His 36 league goals beat Lionel Messi’s 32, and now he has scored more goals than 53 of the 98 teams in Europe’s top five leagues this season.

England is likely to qualify for Euro 2016, but manager Roy Hodgson still seems unsure who his best starting team is. Sportsmail asked their top reporters to pick their ideal starting line-up for the tournament in France, assuming all players are fit. You can share your own England team in the comments below. Matt Lawton’s suggested starting team: Hart; Clyne, Cahill, Jagielka, Baines; Henderson, Wilshere; Welbeck, Rooney, Sterling; Kane.

Hull recovered from their loss to Hull KR on Thursday to win 28-20 at Langtree Park, beating St Helens and ending their third straight defeat. Jamie Shaul scored a long-distance try that secured the win, surprising the home team. St Helens looked tired after their tough match on Good Friday. The injury-plagued champions, who had also lost to Wigan the week before, started with two teenage players in the three-quarter line. Hull saw weaknesses in their defense and took advantage. Fetuli Talanoa (left) celebrated his try as Hull pulled off the unexpected win.

Almeria, who are struggling in La Liga, have appointed former Barcelona player Sergi Barjuan as their third coach this season. The 43-year-old Barjuan replaces Juan Ignacio Martinez, who was fired on Sunday after Almeria lost 4-1 at home to Levante. Almeria said that if all the paperwork is finished, Barjuan will coach the team in their away match against Barcelona on Wednesday. Barjuan played 53 times for Spain between 1998 and 2004. He was a defender at Barcelona for nine years and played in two World Cups for Spain. He also managed Recreativo in Spain’s second division from 2012 to 2014.

Easter Sunday is coming, and Christians across America marked Good Friday, which remembers when Jesus Christ was crucified and died. In places like Ohio, Pennsylvania, and over the Brooklyn Bridge, people walked the "Way of the Cross." These were just a few of many events happening around the world as Holy Week, which started on Palm Sunday, comes to a close. Tens of thousands of people attended Pope Francis' Good Friday torchlight procession at the Colosseum in Rome. During the service, the pope spoke about the persecution of Christians.

While England fans were having a few drinks at the Huntsman pub in Turin on Tuesday afternoon, many went outside to sing an anti-IRA song. The song includes the words “**** the IRA” and continues for a long time. Inside the Juventus Stadium, where about 2,000 England fans were sitting in the north-west section, fans also sang anti-IRA songs during the friendly match against Italy. There is no evidence that the fans shown in the photo were part of the singing.

Many ads in newsagent windows are for things like kittens or handyman services. But one man, known only as John, used the ads to find a partner instead of using online dating. John, a builder, put up a simple ad in the window of his local newsagent in Muswell Hill. He wrote it in big black letters with a pen. The ad says he is looking for someone special and offers "a way of life with quality." A passerby saw it, took a photo, and shared it online. The post quickly spread and became popular.

Helsinborg's manager Henrik Larsson had to put his 42-year-old kit man, Daniel Andersson, in goal on Saturday. Two of his regular goalkeepers, Par Hansson and Matt Pyzdrowski, were injured, so he had no choice. Amazingly, Andersson kept a clean sheet as Helsinborg drew 0-0 with Kalmar in the opening game of the Allsvenskan season. After the game, Andersson told local TV he never expected this. He said he went from being a kit man to goalie coach, and then suddenly had to play in goal. Andersson is a retired goalkeeper who played one game for Sweden in 2001.

Ben Jones-Bishop scored a great solo try as the Salford Red Devils ended a 17-game losing streak against Wigan in a close 24-18 game. Both teams finished with 12 players after fights broke out during the Super League match. Jones-Bishop, who joined Salford from Leeds Rhinos in the summer, now has seven tries this season—the most in the team. Salford led 12-8 at halftime, but Jones-Bishop scored on the hour to help his team move ahead of Wigan into third place in the league table.

It has been just over a year since Alan Pardew had a heated argument with Manuel Pellegrini on the touchline while managing Newcastle. The FA warned Pardew about his actions, and he later wrote to Pellegrini to apologize for calling him an offensive name. On Monday at Selhurst Park, Pardew—now manager of Crystal Palace—will face Pellegrini and Manchester City again. He has worked to change his past behavior, which he thought was becoming harmful. At the advice of the League Managers’ Association, the 53-year-old has had sessions with Jeremy Snape, a former international cricketer who now works as a sports psychologist.

Team news:

Crystal Palace  
Manager Alan Pardew has no new injury worries before the game against Manchester City. However, Marouane Chamakh and Fraizer Campbell are still out with hamstring injuries. Jordon Mutch is also not fit due to a thigh problem.

The title race might seem decided to some, but Joe Hart remains hopeful. He is paid to believe, but there is a good reason for his optimism. Manchester City won the league in 2012 and 2014 by making strong late pushes. "That's kind of how we do it," Hart said when asked about needing to close a nine-point gap. "We like to do things differently. We haven’t been at our best every week, but football gives you another chance. That new chance starts on Monday against Crystal Palace. We have eight important games left to get to the level we need to be."

Mils Muliaina, a rugby player who won the World Cup, has been released on bail after being arrested on suspicion of sexual assault. The former All Black denies the claims. He was arrested last night after his team, Connacht, lost 14-7 to Gloucester in the quarter finals of the European Challenge Cup. Muliaina had been injured during the game and was approached by police at Kingsholm Stadium. The 34-year-old full back, who played 100 times for the All Blacks, was taken away by officers. The arrest relates to an allegation that happened in Cardiff in March. Video is available below.

QPR are feeling confident ahead of their important Barclays Premier League game against Aston Villa on Tuesday. Before Saturday’s match, QPR had lost 13 of their last 14 away league games. But they won 4-1 against West Brom, which ended a five-game losing streak. The win keeps QPR in 19th place, just three points from safety. Coach Chris Ramsey told his players to stay calm during the 4-1 win. Eduardo Vargas (centre) celebrated with his teammates after scoring the first goal against West Brom. "It's a fantastic victory for us," Ramsey said at a press conference on Monday. "The mood is good, and the team has been very professional."

Lydia Ko scored a 2-over 74 on Saturday at the ANA Inspiration. This was her second straight round over par, after she had tied the LPGA Tour record by playing 29 rounds in a row under par. The day before, she hit into the water and took a bogey on the 18th hole, finishing with a 73. On Saturday, she made an 8-foot birdie putt on a par-5 hole, helping her keep a long streak going. The 17-year-old from New Zealand has made at least one birdie in all 187 of her rounds across 49 career events on the tour. "It's always some statistic that catches me," Ko said, not knowing about the birdie streak

Arsene Wenger hasn’t decided yet if he will offer Abou Diaby a new contract, but he has suggested Diaby might stay at Arsenal after this summer. Diaby played in a practice match on Wednesday, marking his latest return from injury. However, he has only played 22 times in the last five seasons at Arsenal, missing long periods due to injuries. Arsenal play Liverpool on Saturday at lunchtime. Wenger probably won’t start Diaby in this important game, but he did say Diaby could earn a new contract, possibly one where he is paid only when he plays.

Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy aren’t playing, but that hasn’t stopped people from coming to the Shell Houston Open in the small town of Humble. A record number of fans have shown up. The event, which is the last tournament before the Masters, is still exciting because of Phil Mickelson’s fun style and local favorite Jordan Spieth. It’s been 18 months since Spieth, who was ranked 809th in the world, left college to play on the PGA Tour. Now, at just 21 years old, he’s ranked fourth in the world. People aren’t criticizing him anymore.
